b1-unit-23.23.1 The ATM kept my card:
Agent: Thank you for calling customer service. My name is Kevin. How can I help you today?
Danny: Hi. I'm calling from Brazil. An ATM here just kept my debit card, and now I'm a little worried.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. Before we start, can I have your date of birth and the last four digits of the card?
Danny: Sure. March third, two thousand four. And the last four digits are six, two, eight, one.
Agent: Thank you. I can see that your card was used at an ATM in São Paulo twenty minutes ago, but no money was taken out.
Danny: That's right. The machine said transaction failed, and then it kept the card.
Agent: OK. I'm going to freeze the card now, so nobody can use it. Unless the bank there gives it back to you today, I'd recommend ordering a new one.
Danny: The problem is, I'm leaving for Argentina in two weeks. Can you send it to Brazil?
Agent: We can, as long as you give us a full address. It usually takes seven to ten business days.
Danny: OK, I'll give you the address of my hostel. In the meantime, how can I get cash?
Agent: Do you have a credit card with us?
Danny: Yes, but I don't want to take out cash with it. The fees are crazy.
Agent: Then a friend could lend you some money, and you can transfer it back to them in the app. Just check the fees first.
Danny: Good idea. And what's my balance right now?
Agent: Your checking account balance is eight hundred forty-two dollars. You're not overdrawn, so don't worry.
Danny: Phew! One more thing. Will you block my new card if I use it in Argentina?
Agent: Not if you tell us your travel dates. You can add them in the app, under travel notice. Otherwise, our system might block the card in case it's fraud.
Danny: Got it. I'll do that tonight.
Agent: Great. Is there anything else I can help you with?
Danny: No, that's all. Thanks so much. You've been very helpful.
Agent: You're welcome. Have a great trip!
